text: Take orders on a register, an iPad or a phone, and add to a check that has already gone to the kitchen.

images.alt: The menu on a phone for table T3: item tiles, category pills, search and a New items button
The check sheet on a phone: items already ordered, new items and a total

text: Send orders to the kitchen screen and to the kitchen and receipt printers. The kitchen sees only what is new.

images.alt: The kitchen screen: order tickets in columns, each with its items and a Bump button
The printers list: a front counter printer and a bar printer

text: Floor plans by room, with the tables where they really are.

images.alt: The floor plan: tables drawn on a grid, coloured by whether they are free, occupied, reserved, cleaning or held

text: Sold-out items marked right on the menu, with the count left (“3 left”) and a “Running Low” flag.

images.alt: The menu on a phone: some items marked Sold out, one marked 3 left and one marked Running Low

text: A time clock with corrections, side work lists, and a shift log for handover notes.

images.alt: The shift log: notes written by people on shift, with a handoff and its reply
The time clock: clocked in, shift so far and the week with a way to request a fix

text: Close the day with a check of open checks and the cash you should have.

images.alt: Closing the day, step one: the checks still open and their total

text: Reports that add up to what each bill actually charged.

images.alt: The Products report: items, quantities and paid subtotals with a total

text: Roles that say who may do what, with every change on the record.

images.alt: Staff roles: the Owner role and its permissions
The change log: who changed what and when, with before-and-after detail

text: Your records stay on a machine you own. Nothing leaves it unless the owner turns it on.
